subject: Discovery recap & infra qualification — SDK/auth/routing + Dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & infra qualification — SDK/auth/routing + Dedicated sizing

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope Dedicated properly:  

Summary of what we covered
- Integration surface: you plan to call Redwood via SDK from an internal service (EHR ingestion pipeline) and also from a customer-facing microservice for guided triage.
- Auth: must use customer-managed keys and VPC Private deployment for PHI.
- Routing: low-latency path for triage (p99 < 300ms for short prompts) and a throughput-heavy batch path for nightly summarization.
- Features required: structured output + tool-calling for actions, embeddings for similarity search, and a reranker for clinical note retrieval.
- Capacity expectations: initial steady-state 100 concurrent small inference calls (1–2s each) and nightly jobs that peak to ~12k tokens/sec for 30 minutes.

Concrete asks / next steps for Horizon (can you confirm by EOD Tue?):
1) Confirm the two traffic classes above (online triage vs nightly batches) and approximate QPS for each.
2) Share any compliance artifacts needed for Private (KMS provider, requirement for HSM, regional constraints).
3) Attach example payload sizes (avg prompt length, avg generated tokens).
4) Approve a 60–90 minute technical workshop next week with Marcus and Marissa to walk the SDK auth flow and Dedicated autoscale options.

I attached a short integration checklist and a first-pass capacity workbook (estimates, not final). Marcus will follow with a proposed autoscale pattern and queueing model.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

— Stephanie

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & infra qualification — SDK/auth/routing + Dedicated sizing

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:  

Traffic classes / numbers
- Online triage: currently expect 60–120 QPS during business hours (peak clinic times). Typical payloads are 150–400 tokens input, expecting ~100–200 tokens generated. P50 latency target is 120–150ms, p95 target < 350ms.
- Nightly batch: our ETL will fan out ~250k records that call embeddings + rerank. We do ~3 batch windows per night, but only one is heavy (30–45 minutes). Peak token ingestion for that window is roughly your 12k tokens/sec estimate.

Compliance
- We require customer-managed KMS and weekly audit logs for inference calls. Also need to know if KV cache persists outside our VPC.

Additional asks
- Can you confirm if the SDK supports token-streaming + structured JSON outputs (we need tool-calling hooks that return validated JSON)?
- For the reranker: do you support on-device quantized embeddings and vector store recommendation, or does that live in Redwood-managed infra under Private?

Happy to run the workshop — Tue/Wed next week works for our infra and security leads.

— Sam Jensen
Director of Engineering, Horizon Health
sam.jensen@horizonhealth.com
[Inline: Horizon compliance questionnaire attached]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & infra qualification — SDK/auth/routing + Dedicated sizing

Sam — thanks for the details, helpful. Short answers up-front, followed by a recommended Dedicated pattern for your two traffic classes.

SDK / Structured output
- Our SDK supports both streaming tokens and evented structured output (tool-calling) that can emit application-validated JSON. We also provide a schema enforcement layer in the SDK to fail fast on invalid tool outputs.

Auth / KMS / KV cache
- Customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own KMS). KV cache only persisted within the Dedicated VPC; it does not live on Redwood public tenancy. Audit logs are available at 7/30/90 day retention tiers.

Embeddings / Reranker
- Embedding generation runs on the same Dedicated nodes (model family selection is configurable). Vector indexing is optional: you can run the vector store in your VPC and call Redwood for embedding-only generation, or use Redwood-managed vector service inside Private for convenience. We can provide quantized embedding binaries for on-prem inference in air-gapped deployments if you opt for on-prem package.

Recommended Dedicated layout (initial size + autoscale)
- Two pools: latency pool (for online triage) and batch pool (for nightly).
- Latency pool: reserved 8x A10 GPUs, min instances 4, max 12. This supports ~100–150 concurrent short requests with p95 under 300ms assuming prompt/generation sizes you listed. Concurrency per GPU is tuned via per-model concurrency limits in the runtime (we suggest starting at 20 concurrent lightweight calls per GPU slot).
- Batch pool: reserved 6x A100-style GPUs, configured for high-throughput kernels and higher batch sizes. Autoscale policy: scale up based on tokens/sec and queue depth; scale down on idle window >10m.
- Queueing: prefer two logical queues per pool (priority/regular). For online triage we recommend a small fast-path queue with bounded concurrency and a fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant if queue depth exceeds threshold.

Attachments: I pushed an initial capacity workbook and a simple infra sequence diagram. These are estimates; workshop will refine.

Next steps from Redwood engineering
- Confirm hardware family preference (A10 vs A100) and whether you want hard SLAs for p95 latency.
- Workshop to validate prompt sizes and run a small SAC test (20k sample prompts) to get realistic token-per-second metrics for your data.

Happy to walk through the workbook in the call.

— Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
